tagline: Infrastructure-free file transfer, screen to camera, speaker to mic — native app.
task: Rebuild the AirLink web prototype (github.com/sarveshadk/airlink, live at airlinkk.vercel.app) as a cross-platform React Native app (iOS + Android) that implements the identical wire protocol, so a phone running this app can send to or receive from the existing web app with zero changes to the frame format.

reference.protocol_version_target: match web prototype, protocol version byte 1 (high nibble of byte offset 1)

core_concept: Sender splits a file into fixed-size chunks, wraps each in a 16-byte header, base45-encodes the frame, and renders it as a repeating QR carousel (or modulates it as audio). Receiver watches/listens continuously, validates every frame against its checksums, and reassembles the file — discarding duplicates across passes. No pairing, no acknowledgement, no back-channel; the receiver can join mid-transmission or drop and rejoin.

fields.notes: high nibble = protocol version, low nibble = frame type
length of the payload that follows
sender's sweep number, mod 256 — makes per-pass loss measurable
CRC-8 over bytes 0-14 — header must be trusted before any field is acted on

encoding.rationale: QR alphanumeric mode packs 5.5 bits/char across 45 symbols; base64 needs lowercase which forces 8-bit byte mode. Base45 carries ~29% more payload per QR symbol at equal CPU cost.

chunking.notes: Header ratio rises with chunk size while P_decode falls with symbol density, so goodput peaks at an interior value. App should expose this as a live-measured curve via the Bench screen, and warn when the current chunk size implies a QR version too dense for typical arm's-length phone cameras.

qr_channel.rationale: Higher EC levels defend against partial symbol damage (paper/ink failure mode). On a screen the failure mode is whole-symbol erasure — the code is located or it isn't — so the carousel's repetition recovers erasures more cheaply than a higher EC level's constant capacity tax. Level H carries ~44% of L's capacity at the same QR version.

audio_channel.approach: data-over-sound, equivalent to the web prototype's ggwave-based channel
audio_channel.notes: No official ggwave React Native binding exists at time of writing. Options: (a) a native module wrapping the ggwave C library for iOS/Android, (b) a WebView bridge loading ggwave.js as a fallback, (c) custom FSK/audio-FFT implementation. Treat as separate milestone from the QR channel; do not block QR-channel completion on this.

retry_strategy.description: Sender cycles through all unacknowledged chunks repeatedly until every chunk is acknowledged or a retry budget expires. Receiver collects opportunistically across passes and discards duplicates.
retry_strategy.back_channel: none — required for the offline/no-pairing property
retry_strategy.shuffle_seed: (transferId, passIndex) — deterministic and reproducible from values already present in the log, no separate permutation needs to be recorded
retry_strategy.shuffle_rationale: A strictly sequential carousel can alias against a periodic receiver blind spot, starving the same chunk indices indefinitely. Per-pass shuffling breaks that lock-in.

reasons.meaning: not an AirLink frame — rejects 255/256 of random data
protocol version this build cannot parse
frame type not in this version's set
fewer payload bytes than payloadLen promised
payload corrupted in transit — runs last, checked over up to 1.5KB
fields disagree with the locked transfer

decode_rejection_reasons.notes: Track counts per category separately — the distribution diagnoses the channel (many bad-magic = camera seeing noise; many bad-payload-crc = frames arriving but corrupted, pointing at distance/gain/frame-rate). Also separate the receiver's own processing losses (camera frames the decoder couldn't keep up with) from true channel losses (frames never decodable).

tech_stack.framework: React Native via Expo (managed workflow) for camera/mic/file-system access without native build friction
tech_stack.camera_and_qr_scan: expo-camera CameraView with built-in barcode scanning (native ML Kit / AVFoundation decode) — a deliberate upgrade over the web prototype's canvas+jsQR loop
tech_stack.qr_generation: react-native-qrcode-svg (supports ecl prop for L/M/Q/H, needed for the EC-level control)
tech_stack.file_system: expo-file-system (chunked reads for send, incremental writes for reassembly)
tech_stack.checksums: crc-32 npm package for CRC-32; small hand-rolled CRC-8 (no package needed, ~10 lines)
tech_stack.base45: base45 npm package, or hand-rolled per RFC 9285 if the package is unmaintained
tech_stack.state_management: zustand for transfer state machine (idle / sending / receiving / complete / error)
tech_stack.navigation: react-navigation bottom tabs: Send, Receive, Bench, Docs
tech_stack.charts_for_live_counters: victory-native, or hand-rolled RN components if a lighter footprint is preferred

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: Landing screen — explain the concept in one line, route to Send/Receive/Bench, show protocol version and app status.

screens.name: Send
screens.purpose: Pick a file and stream it as a QR carousel (or audio, once phase 2 lands).
components: chunk size control (slider or stepper, default 1500B, shows resulting QR version)
live counters: frames sent, passes completed, wire rate (includes headers + repeats), per-frame render cost, current QR version and module geometry

screens.name: Receive
screens.purpose: Continuously scan incoming frames, validate, reassemble, and verify the file.
components: live camera view with scan overlay
chunk grid visualization (filled = received, one cell per chunkIndex) — primary diagnostic for uniform vs. periodic loss
live counters: chunks received, goodput (file bytes/sec, excludes headers+duplicates), duplicate count, per-pass loss rate, camera frame count, symbol miss rate, mean decode time, capture mode
Save / Share button once file is fully reassembled and verified

screens.name: Bench
screens.purpose: Benchmark harness — run controlled transfers and record goodput vs. chunk size / frame rate / EC level, matching the web prototype's Bench tool.

screens.name: Docs
screens.purpose: In-app reference mirroring the protocol spec above, so field testers don't need connectivity to look up the frame format.

permissions_required: media library / file system access for saving received files
non_functional_requirements: Fully offline at runtime: zero network calls once the app is installed — no server, no pairing service, matching the 'no infrastructure' spirit of the original
No secure-context/HTTPS caveat: unlike the web version, native camera APIs need no certificate workaround — call this out explicitly as a platform advantage
Correctness and instrumentation prioritized over visual polish, matching the source project's stated priorities
All 8 decode-rejection categories implemented and tested in the documented cheapest-first order
Shuffle mode must be deterministically reproducible from (transferId, passIndex) alone
Wire-format compatibility: a frame produced by this app's Send screen must be decodable by the existing web app's Receive page, and vice versa
differences_from_web_version: Native barcode scanning (ML Kit / AVFoundation) replaces the canvas+jsQR polling loop — should be faster and more reliable, but decode-timing instrumentation should still be captured for a fair goodput comparison against the web numbers
No HTTPS/secure-context requirement for camera access

Potential access to raw camera frame processors (react-native-vision-camera) if the built-in barcode scanner's decode latency or configurability proves insufficient — treat as a fallback, not the default path
roadmap_after_v1: Adaptive chunk sizing driven by live measured goodput
Optional parity frames for tail-loss recovery (frame types are already reserved for this in the header's type nibble)
Cross-device Bench comparisons against the deployed web app for the research paper's benchmark section
acceptance_criteria: A file sent from this app's Send screen is received correctly by another instance of this app's Receive screen with no network path between them
A file sent from the existing web app (airlinkk.vercel.app/send) is received correctly by this app's Receive screen, proving wire compatibility
Chunk size, frame rate, EC level, and send order are all configurable at runtime and reflected in the live counters
The chunk grid and decode-rejection breakdown are visible and update in real time during a receive session
Checksum verification gates the Save/Share action — no partially-corrupt file can be saved as 'complete'
